about.title: About Tire Speed Calculator
about.description: The Tire Speed Calculator determines vehicle speed based on tire size, gear ratios, and engine RPM. Essential for speedometer calibration, gear ratio selection, and performance analysis. This tool helps understand how tire size changes affect actual vehicle speed, speedometer accuracy, and overall drivetrain performance across different driving conditions.

faq.q: How do larger tires affect speedometer readings?
faq.a: Larger tires make the speedometer read slower than actual speed because the vehicle travels farther per wheel revolution. A 3% tire diameter increase typically causes the speedometer to read 3% low. Our tire speed calculator helps determine exact speedometer error.

faq.q: What gear ratios should I consider for tire size changes?
faq.a: When increasing tire size, consider numerically higher gear ratios to maintain acceleration and engine RPM characteristics. Smaller tires may benefit from numerically lower ratios. Use our calculator to find the optimal balance for your application.

faq.q: How accurate are tire speed calculations?
faq.a: Our tire speed calculations are highly accurate when using precise tire dimensions and gear ratios. Real-world factors like tire pressure, wear, and load can cause minor variations of 1-3% from calculated values.

faq.q: Can this calculator help with transmission selection?
faq.a: Yes, the tire speed calculator shows how different gear ratios affect speed at various RPMs, helping you choose optimal transmission ratios for your tire size, performance goals, and driving conditions.

faq.q: How do I measure tire diameter for accurate calculations?
faq.a: Measure the overall tire diameter from ground to top when properly inflated and loaded. You can also calculate it using tire size markings: rim diameter + (2 × sidewall height). For example, 275/40R18 = 18 + (2 × 4.33) = 26.66 inches.

faq.q: What's the legal speedometer tolerance for tire changes?
faq.a: Most jurisdictions allow speedometer errors within ±10%, but many require accuracy within ±5%. Check local regulations before making significant tire size changes that affect speedometer readings.
